title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Notational inconsistency: (146) defines SR^{0+}_{ρ,σ}, while (147) writes SR^0_{ρ,σ} for (evidently) the same group. The '+' is redundant since Ker Θ ⊂ Ker χ.
(143) uses Z/2 × Z/2 as target while (145)/(146) write μ_2 × μ_2: a harmless identification.
(147) switches from N'_σ to T_σ (ST_σ). This is consistent only if T_σ denotes the neutral torus of N'_σ, so that Ker ε_σ ∩ SN'_σ = ST_σ. This is implicit, not stated on the page.
No substantive mathematical errors are detectable. The decompositions are plausible given the definition (148) of M as (R × SL_2)/μ_2.

ideas.what: Lattice of subgroup schemes of M_{ρ,σ} defined as kernels of characters (det, sign characters) and of the maps to GL_2 and PGL_2, with product decompositions of the 'inner' parts R, SR.
ideas.modern_name: Kernels of characters / component groups of torus normalizers; centralizer decompositions in GL_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard algebraic group theory (Borel, Demazure–Grothendieck SGA3)
ideas.where_published: SGA3 contains the general theory of tori and normalizers; this specific construction is unpublished (Montpellier notes 140-3)

ideas.what: Relating determinants of ρ- and σ-components to det Θ_G up to the sign character ε_3: δ'_σΘ_σ = χ, δ_ρΘ_ρ = ε_3·χ.

deep.surprise_reason: Pure bookkeeping within a larger unpublished construction: kernels of characters and product decompositions of group schemes attached to tori and normalizers in GL_2. Nothing on this page by itself constitutes a new result or connection. The broader context (group schemes attached to GL_2-type solutions of the 'équation des lacets') may be of historical interest, but this page adds only routine definitions.
transcription_corrections: 'd'où les commutations et cocartésiens' should read 'd'où les carrés cartésiens et cocartésiens (99)'.
S'T_ρ is written with a prime (S'T_ρ), consistent with the previous page's 'S^1 T_ρ', which is likely also S'T_ρ.
In (147) the last line reads SR^{0}_{ρ,σ} ≅ ST_ρ × ST_σ × 1 (matching SR^{0+} of (146)).
In (145) the targets are written μ_2 × μ_2 (the image shows a ||μ-like symbol).
